primary_source.title: Implementation Intentions: Strong Effects of Simple Plans

review_method: Verified against Peter M. Gollwitzer (1999), American Psychologist 54(7), 493-503, reviewing empirical trials by Gollwitzer & Brandstätter (1997). Study 2 tasked university students with writing an extensive report on Christmas Eve within 48 hours. Participants who formed concrete implementation intentions (specifying when and where) completed it at a 71% rate, compared to 32% for participants with only a bare goal intention. The psychological mechanism is perceptual readiness and automatic action initiation triggered by situational cues without deliberation. No brain imaging was performed in this study.

claims.paraphrase: 71% of participants with implementation intentions finished a difficult report within 48 hours, compared to 32% with only a goal.
claims.support_summary: p. 496: In Study 2 examining difficult goals (writing a holiday report within 48 hours), 'a full 71% of the participants who had formed implementation intentions did so, whereas only 32% of the participants who had only formed goal intentions succeeded.' (Gollwitzer 1999). 1999 study year on p. 493.

claims.paraphrase: Implementation intentions link situational cues to action initiation, handing control to the environment instead of deliberation.
claims.support_summary: p. 494: 'By forming implementation intentions, people can strategically switch from conscious and effortful control of their goal-directed behaviors to being automatically controlled by selected situational cues.' Linking cues to actions eliminates deliberation.

claims.paraphrase: Holding only a goal intention leaves individuals vulnerable to hesitation, getting derailed by competing demands within 48 hours, or missing opportune moments to act.
claims.support_summary: p. 495: Holding only a goal intention leaves people vulnerable to hesitation, forgetting, or procrastinating over tasks within 48 hours or during busy periods.

claims.paraphrase: Implementation intentions require specifying when and where an action will occur, such as choosing 8 a.m. at a desk.
claims.support_summary: p. 494: Implementation intentions have the structure 'If situation X arises (such as 8 a.m. at my desk), then I will perform response Y!' forming a strong mental link between the specified cue and response initiation.

editorial_suggestions.text: "You waste your Monday freezing at your desk" is our editorial narrative hook, not a finding of the 1999 paper. The paper tested holiday report completion rates, not Monday morning work sessions.
editorial_suggestions.status: creator editorial framing, not a finding of Gollwitzer (1999)

editorial_suggestions.text: "You write 'finish the blueprint' on Monday, yet spend 48 minutes rearranging tabs" is an editorial dramatization illustrating the delay in action initiation. The paper tested writing a report within 48 hours.

The "five-second If-Then lock" is our channel's behavioral heuristic for applying Gollwitzer's implementation intentions to daily work. The 1999 paper tested if-then plans generally, not a five-second rule.
editorial_suggestions.status: creator editorial, not a finding of Gollwitzer (1999)

primary_source.title: Implementation Intentions: Strong Effects of Simple Plans

dossier.experiment_design: Controlled goal-pursuit trials and experiments reviewed by Gollwitzer (1999): participants asked to write a holiday report within 48 hours completed it 71% of the time when they formed an If-Then implementation intention specifying exact time and place, compared to 32% of participants who only set a bare goal intention.
dossier.stat_subtitle: If-Then Plan vs Bare Goal (Gollwitzer 1999, p. 496)
dossier.comparison_text: the If-Then planners finished on time *71%* of the time, versus *32%* with only a goal
dossier.broken_assumption: You set your Monday goal and still freeze at your desk—because deciding *what* you want never tells your mind *when* to start.
dossier.biological_mechanism: Linking a situational cue to a concrete action hands initiation over to the environment instead of deliberation.
dossier.real_world_tax: You write 'finish the blueprint' on Monday, yet spend *48* minutes rearranging tabs before drawing a line.
dossier.willpower_trap: Repeating a vague wish at midnight only deepens hesitation when morning friction hits.
dossier.five_second_override: The *five-second* If-Then lock? Write: *If* it is 8 a.m. at my desk, *then* I draw the *first* line. Comment below your trigger.
dossier.best_hook: You waste your Monday freezing at your desk—a 1999 study proved 71% finish on time, and here is why.
dossier.loop_bridge: Because the moment you mistake a bare Monday wish for a plan...
